newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS sees 1997 group net above 2 billion Sfr.
newsitem.headline: UBS sees 1997 group net above 2 billion Sfr.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland chairman Robert Studer reaffirmed an earlier forecast that group net profit would not be below two billion Swiss francs in 1997.

"It will definitely not be below that," Studer told reporters when asked about a February forecast from chief executive Mathis Cabiallavetta, who said at the time he would be disappointed if profit was not two billion or more.
Studer said a change in the bank's provisioning in 1996 would by itself raise net profit this year to over two billion.

UBS took an extraordinary charge of three billion Swiss francs in 1996 to cover low-risk credit and said the step will reduce its ordinary provisioning from around 1.5 billion francs a year to about 600 million.
Studer said this year's expected drop in ordinary provisions would take net profit over the two billion mark if added to last year's net profit of 1.8 billion before extraordinary items.
Studer declined to comment on expected net profit growth this year beyond the gains from changes in provisions.
